paper.title_en: Carving out the Multifield Cosmological Collider Landscape
paper.abstract_en: We show that inflation with a large number of fields, as predicted by concrete ultraviolet embeddings, generically produces almost-local cosmological collider signals in the bispectrum squeezed limit. We construct the most general boost-breaking mixings between the curvature perturbation and $N_{\rm f}$ additional fields, and extract the late-time scaling dimensions that dictate the soft limits of cosmological correlators. For a handful of fields, an enhanced squeezed limit (with potential oscillations) is a fine-tuned signal. At large $N_{\rm f}\sim100$, however, mixings generically drive the scaling dimensions toward the unitarity boundary. We show that this is a direct consequence of extreme value statistics and random-matrix universality, turning an almost-local bispectrum shape into a generic prediction for almost any masses and mixings.
